### Intraplate deformation within East Asia

**UIUC Department of Earth Science and Environmental Change · Remote**  
Advised by Prof. Lijun Liu

Built a three-dimensional regional model incorporating continental faults and lateral viscosity heterogeneity through data assimilation. The 2023 results indicated the significance of faults for intraplate deformation and suggested sinistral transpression along the Tan-Lu Fault, while not explaining its geological-time dextral transtension.
:::

::: {.project-entry}

### Rock dynamics simulation of planetary crust formation

**USTC School of Earth and Space Sciences · Hefei, Anhui**  
Advised by Prof. Wei Leng, in collaboration with Zhiyi Chen

Used changes in mantle-convection vigor to investigate two-stage planetary crust growth. The work related integrated melting to a crust-growth curve and extended to a hydrated-plume model for ancient continental crust formation. The model results indicated that generating continental crust was nearly impossible with a dry plume, pointing to the importance of deep water in the modeled process.
:::

### African plume influence on Tethys evolution

**USTC School of Earth and Space Sciences · Hefei, Anhui**  
Advised by Prof. Jinshui Huang

Investigated whether the Réunion plume contributed to India's two-stage high-velocity motion toward Eurasia. A coupled plume and double-subduction model better matched the convergence history in the transition between stages, supporting a short-lived but strong plume-push contribution in the model.
:::
:::
